## Works Cited

<!-- works-cited: written by scripts/works-cited.py -->
::: {.works-cited}
Azzara, Christopher D., and Richard F. Grunow. *Developing Musicianship through Improvisation, Book 1: C Instruments*. GIA Publications, 2006. Unit repertoire songs (melody and chords) transcribed into the dmti set of apps/tunes/tunes-object.js: "Mary Ann" (p. 17), "Joshua" (p. 33), "Down by the Riverside" (p. 69); "Long, Long Ago" (p. 1) and "Simple Gifts" (p. 51) were already in the collection. Part 2, Echo Tonal Patterns of Units 4 and 5 (solfège, p. xi), copied into dmti1-unit4-tonal / -unit5-tonal in apps/patterns/pattern-set.js with C as DO (Units 1–3 are the site's major-I-V and minor-i-V); Echo Rhythm Patterns of Units 1–5 (pp. 2, 18, 34, 52, 71; syllables, pp. vii–ix), dmti1-unit1-rhythm … -unit5-rhythm in apps/rhythms/rhythm-pattern-object.js. Reproduced with permission.

Azzara, Christopher D., and Richard F. Grunow. *Developing Musicianship through Improvisation, Book 2: C Instruments*. GIA Publications, 2010. Unit repertoire songs (melody and chords) transcribed into the dmti set of apps/tunes/tunes-object.js: "When the Saints Go Marching In" (p. 1) and "Motherless Child" (p. 39); "Amazing Grace" was already in the collection. Part 2, Echo Tonal Patterns of Units 1–3 (solfège, p. ix; the lower of the two octaves printed), dmti2-unit1-tonal … -unit3-tonal in apps/patterns/pattern-set.js with C as DO (C as LA in Unit 3); Echo Rhythm Patterns of Units 1–3 (pp. 2, 22, 40; syllables, pp. vii–viii), dmti2-unit1-rhythm … -unit3-rhythm in apps/rhythms/rhythm-pattern-object.js. Reproduced with permission.

Azzara, Christopher D., and Richard F. Grunow. *Developing Musicianship through Improvisation, Book 3: C Instruments*. GIA Publications, 2010. Unit 1, "Saint Louis Blues": the twelve Blue Note Patterns (pp. ix, 6), copied into the dmti-blue-notes set of apps/patterns/pattern-set.js with C as DO; the twelve Echo Tonal Patterns of the same page (p. 6, solfège p. ix) are dmti3-unit1-tonal, those of Unit 2 "Transformation" (p. x) dmti3-unit2-tonal and of Unit 3 "Red Wings" (p. xi) dmti3-unit3-tonal (lower octave where two are printed); the Echo Rhythm Patterns of the three units (syllables, pp. vii–viii) are dmti3-unit1-rhythm … -unit3-rhythm in apps/rhythms/rhythm-pattern-object.js. Unit repertoire tunes (melody and chords) transcribed into the dmti set of apps/tunes/tunes-object.js: "Transformation" (p. 23) and "Red Wings" (pp. 47–48), both by Azzara. Reproduced with permission.

Gordon, Edwin E. *Jump Right In: The Music Curriculum. Reference Handbook for Using Learning Sequence Activities*. 2001 revision, GIA Publications, 2001. Tonal sequences (p. 33) and range (p. 32); Tonal Unit 6, partial synthesis (pp. 48–49); Tonal Unit 9, generalization-verbal (pp. 52–54); rhythm patterns and sequences chanted with expressive inflection on one pitch, all durations without pitch ("A Quick Course on Rhythm" and "Techniques for Teaching Class Patterns").

Gordon, Edwin E. *Learning Sequences in Music: A Contemporary Music Learning Theory*. 2012 ed., GIA Publications, 2012. Skill learning sequence: partial synthesis (pp. 111–117), the verbal association warning (p. 108), generalization-aural/oral and -verbal (pp. 131–133); same is easier to hear than different (p. 219); tonal and rhythm patterns kept apart (p. 223); rhythm patterns chanted with vocal inflection like speech (p. 101); macrobeats stressed, not accented, and approached with a decrescendo, expression found between macrobeats, anacruses given special attention, weight and flow, displaced energy in rests and long durations (pp. 187–190).; Theory Concepts pages: Keyality versus key signature (p. xiii); tonality "best refers to what is usually called a mode," the eight tonalities (p. 149); movable-do with la-based minor and the rhythm syllables du de, du da di (p. 105); resting tone and tonic, a tonality in any keyality (p. 150); unitonal and multitonal music (pp. 152, 157); usual duple, triple and combined meter (pp. 175–176); no direct relation between measure signatures and meter, 6/8 as "duple compound" called inaccurate (p. 176); accents and microbeat divisions do not make meter (pp. 176–177); unusual meter, paired and unpaired, intact, macrobeats versus microbeats establishing meter (pp. 179–180); key signatures as do signatures, one signature for many tonalities (pp. 155–156); rhythm syllables by beat function (p. 86); time-value names lead to counting (p. 38); writing tonal patterns from a familiar do signature (p. 125); letter names and time-value names as the alphabet of music (pp. 36–37); interval names learned in context of tonality and keyality (p. 65); the raised seventh of harmonic minor as si (p. 70); mi si ti re as a harmonic minor dominant pattern (p. 100).; Course pages (glossary, enrichment): audiation defined and compared with imitation (Introduction; pp. 3, 9); notation as a window (p. 8); patterns as units of meaning (pp. 99–100); the aural/oral level and the pause (pp. 101–102); discrimination and inference learning, theory delayed (p. 106); levels of the skill learning sequence (from pp. 111, 117, 126, 129, 136, 141); stepwise and bridging movement, Table 17 (pp. 230–231).; Hearing Harmony: four stages of readiness for chord changes (p. 305); harmonic patterns I V7 I, I IV I, I II V7 I, I II7 V7 I (p. 313); I V7 I, then I IV I, then I IV V7 I and I V7 IV I in three sung parts, then harmonic minor (pp. 318–319); easy and moderately difficult harmonic patterns, the supertonic delayed (p. 320).

Grunow, Richard F., Edwin E. Gordon, and Christopher D. Azzara. *Jump Right In: The Instrumental Series. Teacher's Guide for Recorder*. Rev. ed., GIA Publications, 1999. 24 rote songs transcribed into the jri-recorder set of apps/tunes/tunes-object.js (melody and chords), from the piano-accompaniment pages (pp. 258–315). Tonal Patterns from Student Book Two (pp. 321–324; major, minor, Dorian and Mixolydian tonic, dominant and subdominant sets, the minor, Dorian and Mixolydian ones being the site's 322a/b, 323a/b, 324a/b) and the Student Book One tonic and dominant lesson set (pp. 46–47), jri-recorder-tonal-* in apps/patterns/pattern-set.js with C as DO (or LA, RE, SO); Rhythm Patterns from Student Book Two (pp. 325–334), jri-recorder-rhythm-* in apps/rhythms/rhythm-pattern-object.js. Reproduced with permission.

Mullen, Andy. *MLT Any Music Teacher Can Du…De: Teacher's Guide to "The Literate Musician."* The Improving Musician, 2021. Bridging and familiar patterns before unfamiliar ones at generalization (pp. 65–67); the audiation-foundation objectives (p. 74); the tonal sequence (p. 79); partial synthesis in rhythm by naming the microbeat (p. 85); rhythm patterns kept conversational, inflected with style and panache (p. 84).

Mullen, Andy. *The Literate Musician: How to Hear, Speak, Think, Read & Write the Language of Music*. Revised 2nd ed., The Improving Musician, 2020. FPIFO, major and minor tonic and dominant (pp. 57, 59), copied into mullen-fpifo-major / -minor in apps/patterns/pattern-set.js; FPIFO in the Dorian, Mixolydian, Phrygian, Lydian, Aeolian and Locrian tonalities (pp. 22–27), mullen-fpifo-dorian … -locrian, with the keys moved so that C is the book's resting tone; Major and Minor Subdominant FPIFO (p. 293), mullen-subdominant-major / -minor; the stepwise sets (pp. 71–72) are the site's major-stepwise / minor-stepwise; rhythm patterns by lesson (duple and triple macrobeat and microbeat, pp. 37, 39–40; divisions, pp. 45, 47; elongation cells, pp. 48–49), copied into the mullen-rhythm-* sets of apps/rhythms/rhythm-pattern-object.js; translation lessons (Rhythm 8, 9.3, 10.3; Harmony 9); Hearing Harmony: Harmony lessons 2–5 (major and minor tonic and dominant, pp. 53–58), 7 (comparing major and minor, p. 62), the Harmonic Loops by tonality (pp. 20–27). Reproduced with permission.

Reynolds, Alison M., Wendy H. Valerio, Beth M. Bolton, Cynthia C. Taggart, and Edwin E. Gordon. *Music Play: The Early Childhood Music Curriculum; Guide for Parents, Teachers and Caregivers*. GIA Publications, 1998. Part 6, "Developing a Repertoire of Tonal and Rhythm Patterns": tonal acculturation patterns without words, stages 1–3 (p. 24), tonal imitation and assimilation patterns, stages 4–5 (pp. 27–28), and rhythm acculturation (p. 32) and imitation and assimilation patterns (p. 36), copied into musicplay-* sets of apps/patterns/pattern-set.js and apps/rhythms/rhythm-pattern-object.js with C as DO or LA. Reproduced with permission.
